definition: a(1)=1; a(2)=2; then least unused positive m with gcd(m,previous)>1
b_definition: Replace p and 3p by 2p for odd prime p only; 2 and 6 unchanged
interpretation: Numerical evidence only; no mathematical proof of a limiting value
algorithm: Odd composite uint16 smallest-prime-factor sieve; lazy least-unused-multiple cursor per prime; used bitmap; minimum over distinct prime divisors of previous term
correctness_invariant: Each prime cursor starts at p and skips only used multiples; all admissible integers are multiples of prime factors of previous; their minimum is the next term
capacity_policy: Every outside-capacity value is unused; cursors may cross the bound, but selection outside the bound aborts rather than truncating the candidate search
constraints: 4096 <= N <= CAPACITY <= 1000000000; no full sequence stored; real output may differ in its last digits across math libraries
ratio_definition: (b(n)-n)*natural_log(n)/n; signed integer subtraction before long double evaluation; 18 significant output digits
digest_encoding: FNV-1a-64; each a(n) encoded as four little-endian bytes; overflow modulo 2^64
storage_note: Only the first 4096 terms are retained as a sequence. The large arrays are a used bitmap, odd SPF table, and prime cursors; their sizes depend on CAPACITY, not on storing a(N).
rounding_certificate: Exact rational atanh-series bounds for logarithms independently certified that every recorded ratio has absolute error <= 1e-17; displayed nine-decimal paper ratios have absolute error <= 5e-10.
